title: Capacity Signature Suite: synthetic workload orchestrator for dedicated throughput verification
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a reproducible synthetic-workload orchestrator (Capacity Signature Suite) to validate dedicated capacity throughput guarantees, exercise autoscaling policies, and produce customer-facing acceptance artifacts. This ticket covers the harness, a benchmarking methodology that captures tail-latency + cost trade-offs, and a standardized customer acceptance test (CAT) that can be run during Dedicated on-boarding or when proposing SLA changes. The suite intentionally focuses on realistic multi-tenant mixes, KV cache warmup/coldstart scenarios, sequence-length heterogeneity, and autoscaler stress paths rather than purely pushing max QPS at one sequence length.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can run repeatable scenarios defined as 'capacity signatures' with deterministic RNG seeds
Benchmarks produce PVF (percentile, variance, and failure) reports that include p50/p95/p99/p999 latencies and per-token cost estimates
CAT script generates a customer artefact (PDF + JSON) summarizing expected throughput, SLO headroom, and recommended autoscale configs
Harness can reproduce at least three canonical scenarios: cold-KV warmup, hot-cache steady-state, and bursty short-seq traffic with tail-latency focus
Results correlate within ±10% of production probe runs for two pilot customers (pilot-1 and pilot-2)
tasks: Spec: define 'capacity signature' DSL and canonical scenarios
Implementation: lightweight runner with workload templates (http/stream/gRPC), request shaping, and token accounting
Instrument: standardized metrics (per-token cost, CPU/GPU utilization, kernel stalls, KV hit rate) exported to Prometheus/OTLP
Autoscale stress harness: programmable cluster-level policy toggles and synthetic capacity pressure injection
Reporting: PVF report generator and CAT exporter (PDF + machine-readable JSON)
Onboarding: docs and runbook for Solutions Engineers to run CAT during customer validation
design_decisions: Use deterministic seeds + fixed host/time skew to ensure repeatability across runs; this trades some realism for reproducibility
Implement workload templates rather than a full DSL initially to accelerate delivery (templates: baseline, bursty, mixed-length, conversational)
Run most heavy work off-cluster in a separate prober namespace to avoid contaminating control-plane metrics
Favor sampling of kernel-level metrics (1s granularity) over high-frequency tracing to reduce overhead during long runs
Store raw run traces in compressed NDJSON for later audits and reproducibility
test_plan: Unit tests for DSL parsing and deterministic RNG behavior
Integration tests that run short canonical scenarios against staging dedicated clusters (staging-ded-1) with assertions on p95/p99
Calibration runs to map profiler signals to observed cost delta across model variants (FP16 vs 4-bit quant)
Pilot acceptance with two existing dedicated customers to validate correlation and adjust scenario weights
Chaos step: node eviction and model variant fallback during a run to validate graceful degradation and autoscaler reaction
